name: Hotel de Crillon
positioning: Hôtel de Crillon, A Rosewood Hotel: a historic hotel right on Place de la Concorde in Paris, reopened in 2017 after a four-year renovation
best_for: First-time visitors who want to walk to the Tuileries, the Orangerie and the Louvre
Travelers drawn to French history and restored period interiors
Food lovers interested in Paul Pairet's grill and a dedicated pâtisserie

facts.text: The hotel is positioned right on Place de la Concorde.
The Musée de l'Orangerie, the Jardin des Tuileries and the Louvre are all within walking distance.
The building served as a residence for the Count de Crillon until it became a hotel in 1909.
The hotel reopened in 2017 after a four-year renovation led by a team of architects.
Rooms feature custom art, comfortable furnishings and a spacious marble bathroom.
Bar Les Ambassadeurs overlooks Place de la Concorde, has a terrace under the arcades, and serves creative cocktails with live music.
Nonos & Comestibles par Paul Pairet re-invents the French grill.
With Nonos & Comestibles, Paul Pairet unveils his first signature menu in France and Europe since the early 2000s.
From June 1, 2026, Executive Chef Alan Taudon oversees all the dining venues, working closely with Paul Pairet for Nonos & Comestibles.
L'Herbier Secret is an intimate terrace serving plant-based dishes in harmony with coastal inspirations.
Jardin d'Hiver offers all-day dining and afternoon tea, with desserts and teatime by Head Pastry Chef Matthieu Carlin.
The spa also has a grooming salon, a barber and a fitness area.

highlights.text: The Suite Duc de Crillon has original woodwork from the Duc de Crillon's former private chapel; the rest of it is now in New York's Metropolitan Museum.
The restored Grands Appartements were reimagined by Karl Lagerfeld.
The ceiling of Bar Les Ambassadeurs is a registered landmark that the architects restored.
The spa pool is made of 17,000 pieces of gold scales and is lit through a linear glass roof.
Suite Louis XV overlooks the Place de la Concorde, the Eiffel Tower and the Grand Palais.

considerations.text: Four premier rooms are adapted for guests with disabilities.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects its palace hotel status.
WhataHotel notes the formal atmosphere may not suit all travelers.
